chapter: Handedness and Gene Austin in California
title: The 'ambidextrous' newspaper item in Hollywood
summary: Hazel tells how a columnist wrote about his drumming and he misread the word ambidextrous.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: Oh, that's the end of it. A funny little story, Bill, I went, in 34, I went to Hollywood with Gene Austin, you see. Well, I'd rather eat scent for me. The guy out there by the name of Jimmy Stahl was a newspaper columnist, you see. And he wrote it. We were playing at a little private, before we went in the coconut group, played at a private. They had a lot of private clubs out there that were gambling. Places like the Clover Club. Well, we played in a place called the El Rey. And it was strictly a membership deal, you see. And this guy coming in and he saw me playing the cornet and the drums. And he was trying to figure out how I could play the drums half and half. And that's how he goes off and he writes a piece in the Los Angeles paper, you see. And he says something about the drummer, ambidextrously. I never had heard that word in my life before, you know. And I told him, I said, what's that saying about me? I said, I'll rap him, you know. I never had heard ambidextrous in my life. I thought he was saying something bad about me, you know.
How did you play the drums when you played the cornet? Just with your foot?
